chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī Ayyūb, from Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I am occupied. He said: Then do as we do: pray six rakʿahs when the sun is in a position like its position for the ʿaṣr prayer, meaning at the greater rise of the forenoon, and count them as part of the prayers from zawāl.

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: midday decline of the sun, the benchmark for the noon-period nawafil
key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, used here to indicate prayer timing by its position
key_terms.الضُّحَى الْأَكْبَرِ: the later and higher part of the forenoon

ai.seo_question: When can the daytime nawafil be prayed if a person is busy earlier?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal instruction regarding the time of the daytime nawafil for one who is occupied. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that six rakʿahs may be prayed at a later morning time and counted from the nawafil associated with zawāl.
